history.summary: An unusually large 1,302 sqft 2BR at just $913 psf (17% below the $1,102 median) for under $1.19M, sitting 460m from Choa Chu Kang MRT/JRL interchange with a strong 7.3%/yr resale CAGR on 112 transactions. The defining risk is age: 1998 build on a 1995 lease, leaving roughly 68 years — within a decade of the 60-year financing cliff. Low absolute price and JRL catalyst make it interesting, but the lease decay caps the verdict.
history.rating_rationale: The price and PSF look outstanding (913 vs 1,102 median, sub-$1.2M, 1,302 sqft), the txn sample is robust (112) and CCK gets the Jurong Region Line (~2028) plus interchange status — all genuine positives. But the 99-yr lease commenced 1995, so ~68 years remain in 2026; by a 5-7 year exit the buyer faces a ~61-63 year lease nearing the 60-year financing/CPF restriction threshold, which structurally compresses the future buyer pool and is the real reason the PSF is so low. The high historical CAGR partly reflects a low base, not durable quality. D23 is OCR with a ~3.7% baseline; the catalyst helps but does not erase lease decay. Balanced — a value play with a hard ceiling.

history.summary: A real PSF discount on a large unit beside CCK MRT, but accelerating lease decay (~68yrs left), 1998 vintage and a mis-tagged bed count offset the cheapness.
history.rating_rationale: Asking 928 psf sits below the project's entire last-12-month range (966-1198 psf, avg ~1098), so the algo's -16.6% age and -15.7% cohort discounts are real against recent resale evidence (21-txn cohort is reasonable). It is OCR D23 next to Choa Chu Kang MRT/Lot One. However the value is materially offset by lease risk: 99yr from 1995 leaves only ~68 years, where decay and financing/CPF restrictions begin to bite (low_lease and very_old_property flags are genuine, not quirks). The bedroom_sqft_mismatch is explained — a 1055 sqft unit is not a true 1BR but a mis-tagged larger (likely 3BR) layout, so the listing metadata is unreliable and must be re-verified. Cheapness real but lease-shortened: a Neutral hold, not a buy, until the lease/exit math is confirmed for a 5-7yr horizon.

history.summary: A correctly-labelled 1,270 sqft 3BR (bed_bands: ok, 149 contracts) at $1.435M / $1,130 psf in a 762-unit 1998 CapitaLand estate ~460m from the Choa Chu Kang MRT/JRL interchange. It is cheap versus the D23 age-adjusted peer set (-12.8%), but that is mostly the 68-year lease being priced in. Against its own exact-size stack it is at market, not below it.
history.rating_rationale: There is no discount to own comps. 24 same-size (1,259-1,356 sqft) URA prints over the last 24 months cluster around $1.40M / ~$1,105 psf, and this ask is ~2% above that with the floor unknown. The two most recent prints (Jul/Aug-26, low floor) were $883 and $968 psf, so the tape is softening rather than rising. The -12.8% age-adjusted discount to D23 peers is real but is mainly lease decay: 68 years left now, ~61 at a 7-year exit, where CPF/loan pro-rating starts to thin the next buyer pool. That is a ~1%/yr structural drag that roughly cancels the OCR/value tilt. The exit record is middling: REALSCORE 3.6 with only 62.5% of 950 resale pairs profitable (avg 4.0%/yr), a deep sample that says more than a third of past sellers lost money. The positives are real but ordinary: a deep HDB-upgrader buyer pool, 106 URA txns, the MRT/JRL interchange at Lot One, a 3.6% gross yield on 35 rental contracts, and a quantum well inside the $1.8M 'his' mandate. The seller has cut three times ($1.55M Jun, $1.52M Aug, $1.435M now), which signals negotiability. At ≤$1.38M (~$1,085 psf, at or under the stack median) it becomes a fair carry buy on a short lease, but it is not a Buy at the current ask.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: 3.6% gross on 35 URA 3BR contracts in 12mo ($4,300/mo; realsmart median $4,100). It is steady family rental demand near MRT/Lot One. This is carry, not an appreciation signal.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The data 6.9% 5yr CAGR is mostly the 2021-23 re-rating ($770→$1,100 psf). Same-size prints have been flat at ~$1,050-1,170 since late 2023 and are soft in mid-2026. With lease decay steepening, I expect ~1-2.5%/yr nominal forward, below the OCR 3.7% baseline. The ROI projections at ~6.9%/yr are too rosy.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: Floor not disclosed. Same-size prints show floors 11-15 at ~$1,050-1,175 psf vs floors 1-5 at ~$880-1,110. At $1,130 psf the ask is priced like a mid/high floor, so verify the floor before offering. No stack profile has been researched; the estate is 7 blocks of 12 storeys.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Northvale same-size (1,259-1,356 sqft) URA resale prints: flat ~$1,100 psf Nov-23→Aug-26 with softening latest prints. The rate is set below the OCR baseline for the 68→61yr lease decay.
